fruits.extendedStory: If you want the original, it is kept in the town museum. With its cross, the tower reaches 75 metres, a landmark seen from far around. Look for crossed keys among the church's ornaments. They stand for the Archbishop of Bremen. It was Archbishop Giselbert who had the new town built here. You will find the keys in Buxtehude's coat of arms too.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Wer das Original sehen will, findet es im Buxtehude Museum. Mit dem Kreuz ist der Turm 75 Meter hoch und weithin zu sehen. Achte auf die gekreuzten Schlüssel in den Verzierungen der Kirche. Sie stehen für den Bremer Erzbischof. Erzbischof Giselbert ließ hier die neue Stadt bauen. Auch im Buxtehuder Stadtwappen findest du sie.
localizedExtendedStory.en: If you want the original, it is kept in the town museum. With its cross, the tower reaches 75 metres, a landmark seen from far around. Look for crossed keys among the church's ornaments. They stand for the Archbishop of Bremen. It was Archbishop Giselbert who had the new town built here. You will find the keys in Buxtehude's coat of arms too.

localizedStory.de: Schau hoch zur Wetterfahne. Seepferdchen nennen die Buxtehuder das Tier, dabei sieht es aus wie ein Drache. Was es wirklich ist, weiß niemand genau.
localizedStory.en: Look up at the tower's weathervane. Locals call the beast the seahorse, though it looks like a dragon. Nobody is quite sure which it is.

fruits.name: St. Petri-Kirche
fruits.story: Look up at the tower's weathervane. Locals call the beast the seahorse, though it looks like a dragon. Nobody is quite sure which it is.

fruits.extendedStory: Look for a stone on its east side with the town arms and the year 1539. Yet tree rings from logs under the vanished Linah-Zwinger, its sister tower, point to the 1550s. So stone and wood disagree. Every citizen whose house backed onto the wall had to look after his own stretch of it. The museum society once bought the partly collapsed tower to save it, and today it hosts concerts and exhibitions.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Such an der Ostseite einen Stein mit dem Stadtwappen und der Jahreszahl 1539. Baumringe von Hölzern unter dem verschwundenen Linah-Zwinger, seinem Schwesterturm, deuten aber auf die 1550er Jahre. Stein und Holz sind sich also nicht einig. Jeder Bürger, an dessen Haus die Mauer grenzte, musste seinen eigenen Abschnitt in Schuss halten. Einmal kaufte der Museumsverein den teils eingestürzten Turm, um ihn zu retten. Heute gibt es hier Konzerte und Ausstellungen.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Look for a stone on its east side with the town arms and the year 1539. Yet tree rings from logs under the vanished Linah-Zwinger, its sister tower, point to the 1550s. So stone and wood disagree. Every citizen whose house backed onto the wall had to look after his own stretch of it. The museum society once bought the partly collapsed tower to save it, and today it hosts concerts and exhibitions.

localizedStory.de: Von fünf runden Türmen der Stadtmauer ist dieser übrig geblieben. Er hat schon Jugendherberge gespielt und sogar Rettungsschwimmer beherbergt.
localizedStory.en: Five round towers once stood on the town wall, and this is the last. It has even been a youth hostel and a lifeguards' clubhouse.

fruits.name: Marschtorzwinger
fruits.story: Five round towers once stood on the town wall, and this is the last. It has even been a youth hostel and a lifeguards' clubhouse.

fruits.extendedStory: He had heard it in Bexhövede, from an old hunter. Later the Brothers Grimm took the race into their fairy-tale collection, as number 187. Fritz Fleer made the sculptures here in 1968. Buxtehude's fairy-tale society and many donors made the fountain happen. Look for the hare, caught in the middle of his run.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Gehört hatte er sie in Bexhövede, von einem alten Jäger. Später nahmen die Brüder Grimm den Wettlauf in ihre Kinder- und Hausmärchen auf, als Nummer 187. Die Figuren schuf Fritz Fleer im Jahr 1968. Möglich gemacht haben den Brunnen die Buxtehuder Märchengesellschaft und viele Spender. Schau dir den Hasen an, mitten im Lauf.
localizedExtendedStory.en: He had heard it in Bexhövede, from an old hunter. Later the Brothers Grimm took the race into their fairy-tale collection, as number 187. Fritz Fleer made the sculptures here in 1968. Buxtehude's fairy-tale society and many donors made the fountain happen. Look for the hare, caught in the middle of his run.

localizedStory.de: Wilhelm Schröder, der diese Geschichte erzählte, hörte sie bei Bremerhaven. Den Wettlauf von Hase und Igel verlegte er aber nach Buxtehude. Niemand weiß, warum.
localizedStory.en: Wilhelm Schröder, the man who told this tale, heard it near Bremerhaven. Yet he set the hare and hedgehog's race in Buxtehude. Nobody knows why.

fruits.name: Hase-und-Igel-Brunnen
fruits.story: Wilhelm Schröder, the man who told this tale, heard it near Bremerhaven. Yet he set the hare and hedgehog's race in Buxtehude. Nobody knows why.

fruits.extendedStory: Mills have stood on this spot since shortly after the town was founded, driven by the dammed-up river Este. Flat-bottomed cargo boats sailed up the Fleth and turned in the basin in front of the mill. They came to load, to unload or to have grain ground. A surviving Ewer, the Margareta, shows how such boats were built: its mast lowers to pass under the fixed bridges. Raised several times, the brick mill now holds homes, shops and a hotel.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Seit kurz nach der Stadtgründung stehen an dieser Stelle Mühlen, angetrieben von der aufgestauten Este. Plattbodige Frachtschiffe kamen das Fleth herauf und wendeten im Becken vor der Mühle. Sie luden Waren auf oder ab oder ließen Getreide mahlen. Wie solche Schiffe gebaut waren, zeigt ein erhaltener Ewer namens Margareta. Sein Mast lässt sich umlegen, damit er unter den festen Brücken durchpasst. Die Backsteinmühle wurde mehrmals aufgestockt und beherbergt heute Wohnungen, Läden und ein Hotel.

A surviving Ewer, the Margareta, shows how such boats were built: its mast lowers to pass under the fixed bridges. Raised several times, the brick mill now holds homes, shops and a hotel.

localizedStory.de: An der Schleuse standen einst kleine Pfahlhütten über dem Wasser. Es waren Toiletten, abgerissen erst 1964.
localizedStory.en: Little huts on stilts once stood over the water by the lock. They were toilets, and they were not torn down until 1964.

fruits.name: Flethmühle Buxtehude
fruits.story: Little huts on stilts once stood over the water by the lock. They were toilets, and they were not torn down until 1964.

fruits.extendedStory: Down at the door, the columns show hare and hedgehog, and also a bell and a dog. The story goes that Dutch settlers rang Buxtehude's bells with a rope, while other towns still struck theirs with a hammer. In their tongue, so the tale goes, a bell was a 'hunte' and ringing was 'bellen'. In German, 'Hund' is a dog and 'bellen' means to bark. And the rope, they say, soon looked like a tail, hence the saying that here dogs bark with their tails.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Unten am Eingang zeigen die Säulen Hase und Igel, dazu eine Glocke und einen Hund. Der Sage nach läuteten die niederländischen Siedler in Buxtehude ihre Glocken mit einem Seil, als andere Städte noch mit dem Hammer schlugen. Auf Niederländisch, so erzählt man, hieß die Glocke Hunte und läuten hieß bellen. Und das Seil sah bald aus wie ein Schwanz, sagt man. Darum heißt es: In Buxtehude bellen die Hunde mit dem Schwanz.

The story goes that Dutch settlers rang Buxtehude's bells with a rope, while other towns still struck theirs with a hammer. In their tongue, so the tale goes, a bell was a 'hunte' and ringing was 'bellen'. In German, 'Hund' is a dog and 'bellen' means to bark. And the rope, they say, soon looked like a tail, hence the saying that here dogs bark with their tails.

localizedStory.de: Schau über den Balkon. Dort späht ein Turmwächter aus einem Fenster, das es gar nicht gibt.
localizedStory.en: Look up above the balcony. A tower watchman peeks out of a make-believe window.

fruits.name: Rathaus Buxtehude
fruits.story: Look up above the balcony. A tower watchman peeks out of a make-believe window.

fruits.extendedStory: He is an older man, life-size, standing at the railing and looking back over his shoulder into the water. He stands for the real men who once raised the alarm at high water and watched how deep it ran. Carsten Eggers modelled him in 1989 to look true to life, then had him cast in bronze. Stand next to him and follow his gaze.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Ein älterer Mann in Lebensgröße steht am Geländer und blickt über die Schulter ins Wasser hinter sich. Er erinnert an die echten Männer, die bei Hochwasser Alarm schlugen und auf die Wassertiefen achteten. Carsten Eggers hat ihn 1989 lebensecht modelliert und dann in Bronze gießen lassen. Stell dich neben ihn und folge seinem Blick.
localizedExtendedStory.en: He is an older man, life-size, standing at the railing and looking back over his shoulder into the water. He stands for the real men who once raised the alarm at high water and watched how deep it ran. Carsten Eggers modelled him in 1989 to look true to life, then had him cast in bronze. Stand next to him and follow his gaze.

localizedStory.de: Schau auf die Hand des Bronzemanns. Sie ist blank gerieben, denn man sagt, er bringe Glück.
localizedStory.en: Look at the bronze man's hand. It is rubbed shiny, because people say he brings luck.

fruits.name: Fleetenkieker
fruits.story: Look at the bronze man's hand. It is rubbed shiny, because people say he brings luck.
